types.name: Physical payload
types.desc: abd_t: the bytes exactly as they sit on disk (compressed / encrypted / padded to ashift).

types.name: ARC buffer
types.desc: arc_buf_t / arc_buf_hdr_t: cached block, keyed by DVA + birth txg.

types.name: I/O request
types.desc: zio_t moving through the pipeline (logical zio or a vdev child zio).

types.name: Block pointer
types.desc: blkptr_t: DVAs + sizes + checksum + birth txg. The address of a block.

types.name: Transaction
types.desc: dmu_tx_t membership / a txg number being opened, quiesced or synced.

types.name: Device I/O
types.desc: struct bio (Linux) / GEOM bio (FreeBSD): sector I/O at the block device.

types.name: Control
types.desc: Calls that carry no payload: locks, wakeups, throttling, accounting, callbacks. Draw dashed.

types.name: Scan work
types.desc: Scan state and work items: bookmarks, the dataset queue, queued scan entries (sios) and extents, scan position and counters.

types.name: Dirty time log
types.desc: DTL range trees: the txg ranges a device is missing, and checks against them.

contexts.name: Kernel, in the thread of the calling process (an ioctl on /dev/zfs, mount(2) or umount(2)) or a helper thread it starts, outside syncing context and outside any dmu_tx
Syncing context: txg_sync thread or dp_sync_taskq workers, one txg at a time
zio issue taskq (z_wr_iss, z_rd_iss, z_fr_iss ...): CPU work - compress, checksum, allocate
zio interrupt taskq (z_wr_int, z_rd_int ...): completion processing
A dedicated kernel thread or zthr
Runs in whichever context calls it

groups.title: Userspace (zpool, libzfs)
groups.summary: The commands that start, pause, stop and report a scan, and attach or replace a device.

groups.title: Kernel entry, spa and async work
groups.summary: ioctl handlers, the spa entry points and the async thread that starts resilvers and detaches replaced devices.

groups.title: TXG sync and scan state
groups.summary: The txg sync thread, sync tasks that change the scan, and the scan state kept in the MOS.

groups.title: dsl_scan traversal (syncing context)
groups.summary: Per-txg metadata walk that finds the blocks to read.

groups.title: Sequential rebuild (vdev_rebuild)
groups.summary: Per-top-level-vdev thread that copies allocated space in LBA order.

groups.title: Sorted scan queues and issue
groups.summary: Per top-level vdev queues that turn the traversal's random order into offset order.

groups.title: Error scrub (zpool scrub -e)
groups.summary: Reads only the blocks listed in the pool's error log.

groups.title: ZIO pipeline
groups.summary: The read pipeline every scan I/O walks; shared with the I/O flow graph.

groups.title: DTL - dirty time logs
groups.summary: What each device is missing, and how that steers resilver and repair.

groups.title: VDEV tree + queues
groups.summary: Mirror and raidz read and repair logic, per-disk queues, and I/O accounting.

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.role: The person or script typing the command. Every path in this graph that a command starts begins with a wire from this node; the arrows that come back into a command node are its results, errors and refusals.

nodes.title: zpool scrub / zpool resilver
nodes.role: `zpool scrub` options: `-p` pause, `-s` stop, `-e` error scrub, `-t` thorough (decompress and decrypt what is read), `-S`/`-E` start and end dates, `-C` continue from the last completed scrub's txg, `-w` wait. `zpool resilver` asks for a resilver to restart. Each pool is handled by scrub_callback().

nodes.title: zpool attach / replace
nodes.role: Adds a mirror side or replaces a device. Without `-s` the new device is filled by a healing resilver; with `-s` by a sequential rebuild.

nodes.title: libzfs / libzfs_core
nodes.role: Packs the request into an nvlist (scan_type, scan_command, scan_flags, optional dates) for ZFS_IOC_POOL_SCRUB, or a zfs_cmd_t for ZFS_IOC_VDEV_ATTACH.

nodes.title: zpool status (scan line)
nodes.role: Reports "scanned" (bytes examined by the traversal), "issued" (bytes whose read was sent) and "repaired" or "resilvered" (bytes written by repair writes). Percent done and the time estimate come from issued bytes and the issue rate, so a scan that is still traversing shows no estimate. Rebuilds are reported per top-level vdev.

nodes.title: zfs_ioc_pool_scrub()
nodes.role: Validates the request and routes it: pause, stop, or start with a txg range. Dates are turned into txgs through the pool's txg time log, `-C` starts at the txg the last completed scrub ended at.

nodes.title: spa_scan_range() / spa_scan_stop() / spa_scrub_pause_resume()
nodes.role: Checks before the dsl layer: a txg range only for a scrub; a requested resilver needs the resilver_defer feature enabled and does nothing but request SPA_ASYNC_RESILVER_DONE when no leaf has a DTL; an error scrub needs the head_errlog feature; pause and stop return EBUSY while a resilver runs.

nodes.title: dsl_scan() / dsl_scan_cancel()
nodes.role: Open-context side of the scan. dsl_scan() first reopens and probes every vdev, then: a resilver only sets scn_restart_txg (dsl_scan_restart_resilver()), a paused scrub or error scrub is resumed, anything else queues a setup sync task. Cancel and pause also go through sync tasks. dsl_scan_restart_resilver() is also called by the async thread and by attach.

nodes.title: spa_vdev_attach()

ref.code: spa_vdev_attach(spa_t *spa, uint64_t guid, nvlist_t *nvroot, int replacing,

nodes.role: Adds the new device under a mirror, replacing or spare vdev, marks it as missing every txg so far, and starts a resilver (or defers it) or, with `-s`, a rebuild.

nodes.title: spa_async_thread()
nodes.role: Background worker for requests that need locks sync context cannot take: SPA_ASYNC_RESILVER restarts a resilver, SPA_ASYNC_RESILVER_DONE and SPA_ASYNC_REBUILD_DONE detach finished replacements.

nodes.title: vdev_open() resilver check
nodes.role: Every time a leaf is opened (import, online, clear, reopen) its DTL is checked. Missing txgs start a resilver, or are deferred, unless the open is the probe a starting scrub does (spa_scrub_reopen).

nodes.title: spa_vdev_resilver_done()

ref.code: spa_vdev_detach(spa_t *spa, uint64_t guid, uint64_t pguid, int replace_done)

nodes.role: Finds replacing and spare vdevs whose new device is complete and detaches the old device (and the hot spare it replaced), which ends a `zpool replace`.

nodes.title: TXG: syncing (txg_sync_thread)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Normally waits up to zfs_txg_timeout between txgs; while dsl_scan_active() is true (a scan running and not paused, or frees pending) it syncs the next txg at once, so the scan gets a slice of every txg. Sync tasks that set up, pause or cancel a scan wait here for their txg.

nodes.title: spa_sync()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Each sync pass runs dsl_pool_sync() (which executes queued sync tasks), then dsl_scan_sync() and dsl_errorscrub_sync(), then vdev_sync() for dirty top-level vdevs, which writes changed DTLs.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_setup_sync()
nodes.role: Starts a scan in syncing context. Refused (EBUSY) while a scan, rebuild or error scrub runs. Resets scn_phys, records the txg range (a resilver's range comes from the DTLs), rewrites all labels, creates the dataset queue object and posts a scrub or resilver start event. The error scrub variant points a cursor at the last error log instead.

nodes.title: Pause / resume / cancel tasks
nodes.role: Sync tasks for `zpool scrub -p`, a resume, and `zpool scrub -s`. Pause only sets DSF_SCRUB_PAUSED: the queues and bookmark stay, and the scan continues where it was when resumed.

nodes.title: Scan state in the MOS (scn_phys)
nodes.role: dsl_scan_phys_t in the pool directory: function, state, txg range, bookmark, DDT bookmark, counters (to_examine, examined, skipped, processed, errors). It is written only when the sorted queues are empty, so after an import a scan restarts from its last checkpoint. dsl_scan_init() reloads it at import.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_done()
nodes.role: Ends a scan, completed or cancelled: frees the dataset queue and sorted queues, reassesses DTLs, sets the final state, rotates the error log, asks the async thread to detach finished replacements and to start a deferred resilver if one is due.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_sync()
nodes.role: The per-txg driver, sync pass 1 only. Restarts the scan when scn_restart_txg is reached, waits zfs_import_defer_txgs after an import, runs async destroys first, does nothing while paused. Then, for a sorted scan, decides from queue memory and the checkpoint timer whether this txg traverses metadata or issues queued reads; never both. When traversal is complete and the queues are empty, it ends the scan.

nodes.title: Per-txg time limit
nodes.role: After the minimum time (750 ms scrub, 1500 ms resilver by default) the scan yields when dirty data reaches zfs_vdev_async_write_active_min_dirty_percent of zfs_dirty_data_max, when someone waits for the txg, or when zfs_txg_timeout has passed since the txg started; always when the pool is exporting. So application writes and `sync` shorten each scan slice.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_visit() / dataset queue
nodes.role: Order of the walk: the DDT pass, then the MOS, then $ORIGIN, then datasets from the in-memory queue. After a dataset is finished its next snapshot and its clones are queued with the creation txg as their lower bound, so each later snapshot is only searched for blocks born after the previous one. Also scans the head dataset's ZIL blocks.

nodes.title: DDT pass (dsl_scan_ddt)
nodes.role: Before the tree walk, a scrub or resilver reads every dedup table entry with more than one reference once (when the scan has a start txg, only the obsolete ditto class), so the tree walk can skip those blocks however many files point to them.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_visitbp() recursion
nodes.role: Depth-first walk of one block tree. Skips holes and every block not born after cur_min_txg (its whole subtree is older), reads indirect, dnode and objset blocks synchronously to find their children, and hands each block, metadata included, to the scan callback. On resume, subtrees before the bookmark are skipped.

nodes.title: Scan prefetch thread
nodes.role: Runs on dp_sync_taskq beside the traversal. Reads indirect, dnode and objset blocks ahead of it into the ARC (never level-0 data), so the traversal's synchronous reads are cache hits. Shares scn_maxinflight_bytes (zfs_scan_vdev_limit x data disks, at most a quarter of the ARC maximum).

nodes.title: dsl_scan_scrub_cb()
nodes.role: Decides whether a block is read. Blocks born outside (scn_min_txg, scn_max_txg) are only counted. A scrub reads every other block; a resilver only those that dsl_scan_need_resilver() selects. Sets the zio flags: SCRUB or RESILVER, SCAN_THREAD, CANFAIL, and RAW unless the scrub is thorough.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_need_resilver()
nodes.role: Per DVA: does the top-level vdev holding it have a DTL that covers the block's physical birth txg (for raidz: on a child holding part of the block), and is at least one leaf under it not deferred? Blocks on vdevs with no missing data are skipped, which is why a resilver of a mostly-current device is short.

nodes.title: vdev_rebuild()
nodes.role: Starts a rebuild of one top-level vdev (mirror or dRAID): a sync task activates the device_rebuild feature, records the DTL txg range and creates the rebuild thread. If one is already running it is reset to include the new device.

nodes.title: vdev_rebuild_thread()
nodes.role: Walks the top-level vdev's metaslabs in order. Each metaslab is disabled for allocation, its allocated ranges are loaded from the space map, and they are rebuilt in LBA order. Block pointers and checksums are never looked at, and data held only by a checkpoint is rebuilt too. Progress is kept per top-level vdev, so rebuilds of different vdevs are independent.

nodes.title: vdev_rebuild_range()
nodes.role: Issues one rebuild read for a chunk of allocated space, described by a made-up block pointer with checksum off, and records the progress offset per txg.

nodes.title: vdev_rebuild_complete_sync()
nodes.role: Marks the rebuild complete, excises the DTLs, requests the detach of the replaced device and, when no other scan runs, starts a scrub to verify checksums.

nodes.title: dsl_scan_enqueue()
nodes.role: Sorted scan: one queue entry per DVA, in the queue of the top-level vdev that DVA is on, carrying all DVAs so a repair can use the other copies. Legacy scans and gang blocks are read at once instead.

nodes.title: Scan queue per top-level vdev
nodes.role: Entries (sios) sorted by offset, plus extents: offset ranges merged across gaps up to zfs_scan_max_ext_gap and scored by size and fill. Its memory is what decides between traversing and issuing. A block freed while queued is removed.

nodes.title: scan_io_queues_run()
nodes.role: One thread per top-level vdev on the dsl_scan_iss taskq, while dsl_scan_sync() waits. Each picks extents and issues their entries in offset order until the time limit. Strategy (zfs_scan_issue_strategy): 0 = best extents first while clearing memory, LBA order while checkpointing; 1 = always LBA order; 2 = always best first.

nodes.title: scan_exec_io()
nodes.role: Creates the scan read. Waits while the queue's bytes in flight are at zfs_scan_vdev_limit x data disks of that top-level vdev (pool-wide limit for legacy and error scrub reads). Counts issued bytes. The read goes straight to zio_read() with its own buffer: scan data never enters the ARC.

nodes.title: dsl_errorscrub_sync()
nodes.role: Walks the last error log instead of the pool. With head_errlog it reads the block in the head dataset when it is unchanged and in the snapshots that still hold that version. Runs in sync pass 1 after dsl_scan_sync(); a resilver cancels it. When the log is done, the error log is rotated: the errors found by this pass replace the previous log, so blocks that now read cleanly drop out of `zpool status -v`.

nodes.title: read_by_block_level()
nodes.role: Looks up the block's current block pointer through the dnode (needs the dataset's key if encrypted) and issues it as a scrub read.

nodes.title: arc_read()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Used by the traversal and the prefetch thread for metadata only, at ZIO_PRIORITY_SCRUB. Data blocks read by the scan do not pass through the ARC.

nodes.title: zio create + execute
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Scan reads are ordinary zio_read() calls with scan flags; each txg's scan reads hang under a root zio that dsl_scan_sync() waits for.

nodes.title: READ_BP_INIT
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Queues decompress and decrypt for the completion, except for RAW reads: a normal scrub only verifies the stored bytes, a thorough scrub also decompresses and decrypts them.

nodes.title: READY
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. A read passes straight through.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_START
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Routes the zio down the vdev tree. A repair write without SELF_HEAL is skipped on a vdev whose DTL says it is not missing that txg. A leaf that is not accessible fails the zio with ENXIO without touching the disk.

nodes.title: FREE stages

ref.code: zio_free_sync(zio_t *pio, spa_t *spa, uint64_t txg, const blkptr_t *bp,

nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Before space is returned to its metaslab, the scan is told so it can drop a queued read of that block.

nodes.title: zio taskqs (issue / interrupt)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Completions continue on an interrupt taskq.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_DONE
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Releases the queue slot and lets the mirror or raidz code inspect its children: this is where bad copies are found and repair writes are created.

nodes.title: VDEV_IO_ASSESS
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. A failed leaf zio is turned into ENXIO when the device is no longer accessible; child zios are not retried.

nodes.title: CHECKSUM_VERIFY
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Runs in each child that carries the block pointer (mirror sides, plain disks). A mismatch increments the device's checksum error count and starts a checksum ereport. Raidz checks the checksum itself in vdev_raidz_io_done().

nodes.title: DONE
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Updates per-vdev statistics, runs the done callback (scan, rebuild) and notifies the parent.

nodes.title: vdev_dtl_dirty()

ref.code: vdev_dtl_dirty(vdev_t *vd, vdev_dtl_type_t t, uint64_t txg, uint64_t size)

nodes.role: Adds a txg range to one of a vdev's four DTLs. DTL_MISSING: txgs the vdev has no valid copy of. DTL_PARTIAL: txgs not fully replicated below it. DTL_SCRUB: txgs a running scan could not repair. DTL_OUTAGE: txgs that cannot be read right now. Only the leaves' DTL_MISSING is stored on disk.

nodes.title: DTL range checks

ref.code: vdev_dtl_contains(vdev_t *vd, vdev_dtl_type_t t, uint64_t txg, uint64_t size)

nodes.role: The questions asked of DTLs: does this vdev miss txg N, does any writable leaf need resilver and for which range, does this block's DVA touch a dirty child, and can this device be detached without losing data.

nodes.title: Resilver deferral
nodes.role: With the resilver_defer feature enabled, a device that needs resilver while one is running is flagged instead of restarting the running resilver from the beginning. Its DTL is not cleared by the running resilver; a second resilver starts for it when the first ends.

nodes.title: vdev_dtl_reassess()
nodes.role: Recomputes DTLs bottom up. After a completed scan that had no errors or was started since the pool was imported (a rebuild: that had no errors), a leaf that is at least degraded, not deferred and, if it was attached for this resilver, whose DTL ends inside the scanned range gets DTL_MISSING below the scan's max txg replaced by DTL_SCRUB, the txgs the scan could not repair. Interior vdevs derive theirs from the children: a mirror misses a txg only when every child does, raidz when more than nparity children do.

nodes.title: vdev_dtl_sync()

ref.code: vdev_dirty(vdev_t *vd, int flags, void *arg, uint64_t txg)

nodes.role: Writes a leaf's DTL_MISSING to its own space map object in the MOS when it changed in this txg, so missing txgs survive a reboot.

nodes.title: DVA fan-out (copies / ditto)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. For a scan read the logical zio's DVAs are treated as mirror sides. A sorted scrub checks only the first DVA, because each DVA has its own queued entry; the other copies are kept for repair.

nodes.title: Mirror vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Scrub: reads every readable child and keeps a buffer for each. Resilver and rebuild: read one child that is not missing the data. On completion it rewrites children that returned errors and, for a resilver, children whose DTL has the txg. Replacing and spare vdevs are mirrors too.

nodes.title: RAIDZ / dRAID vdev
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Scrub and resilver read all data and parity columns. The whole block is checked against its checksum here; if it fails, every column is read and combinations of columns are rebuilt from parity until the checksum matches. Unused parity is verified too, and wrong or missing columns are rewritten.

nodes.title: zio_vdev_child_io()
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Creates the read or repair-write child for one vdev below; a child with a block pointer checks the checksum itself.

nodes.title: Per-disk I/O queue
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Scan reads use the scrub class, rebuild reads the rebuild class, repair writes the async write class. Scrub and rebuild are non-interactive: while sync or async I/O is active on the disk they get their min_active, and at most zfs_vdev_nia_credit of them are sent while interactive I/O is outstanding; only after zfs_vdev_nia_delay of them complete on an otherwise idle disk do they get max_active.

nodes.title: Leaf vdev driver
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Turns the zio into a block-device request.

nodes.title: I/O completion
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. Records the result and re-enters the pipeline on an interrupt taskq.

nodes.title: vdev_stat_update()
nodes.role: Per-vdev accounting at the end of every zio. Successful repair writes are counted as scan progress (scn_processed) or rebuild progress (vrp_bytes_rebuilt). Failed writes are recorded in the DTLs.

nodes.title: Data disks (normal class)
nodes.role: Shared with the I/O flow graph. The pool's disks; scan reads and repair writes land here (and on special and dedup vdevs, which are not drawn separately).

model: A scrub or resilver runs inside txg sync. Once per txg, in sync pass 1, `dsl_scan_sync()` works for a time slice (at least `zfs_scrub_min_time_ms` or `zfs_resilver_min_time_ms`) and saves its position as a bookmark. While a scan is active the txg sync thread does not wait for `zfs_txg_timeout`, so txgs follow each other back to back.

A scan has two phases that alternate between txgs, never both in one txg: metadata traversal ("scanned" in `zpool status`), which reads indirect, dnode and objset blocks through the ARC in logical order and collects every block pointer in the txg range, and issue ("issued"), which reads the collected blocks sorted by disk offset per top-level vdev. Which phase runs depends on how much memory the queues use.

Scrub and resilver are the same traversal and the same read. A scrub reads every block born in its range; a resilver reads only blocks whose birth txg is in the DTL of some leaf device. Snapshots are walked oldest first and a block older than the previous snapshot is skipped, so a block shared by many snapshots is read once.

Repair happens in the vdev layer, not in the scan code. A scrub read on a mirror reads every child and on raidz every data and parity column; the checksum in the block pointer identifies the bad copy, and the good data is written back as a repair write. Successful repair writes are what `zpool status` reports as "repaired" or "resilvered".

A DTL is a per-leaf list of txgs the device is missing. It grows when a write cannot reach the device, steers which copies a read may use, decides what a resilver reads, and is rewritten from what the scan could not repair when the scan completes.
Scan I/O is background I/O: the scrub class in each disk's queue gets its full `zfs_vdev_scrub_max_active` only while no interactive I/O is active on that disk.
A sequential rebuild (`zpool attach -s`, `zpool replace -s`, dRAID spares) copies allocated space in LBA order without block pointers or checksums, then starts a scrub to verify what it copied.
simplifications: The shared zio and vdev nodes show only the stages scan I/O uses. Gang blocks, embedded block pointers and dedup reads are not drawn; gang blocks are read during the traversal and never queued.
Async destroys, the ZIL scan (dsl_scan_zil()) and the DDT walk's interaction with dedup reference changes run inside dsl_scan_sync() but are only mentioned in node text.
Indirect blocks are both traversed (read through the ARC) and handed to the scan callback, so they are verified like data; the paths show one data block.
Extra copies (copies=2/3, metadata ditto blocks) each get their own queued read; repair from another DVA uses the same DVA fan-out as the I/O graph and is not drawn as a separate alternative.
dRAID is folded into the raidz node; distributed spares, dRAID-specific DTL checks and raidz expansion are left out.
Dataset changes during a scan (destroy, new snapshot, clone swap) adjust the saved bookmark and queue; they are not drawn.
A pool checkpoint stops a completed scrub or resilver from excising DTLs; a rebuild still does. Device removal (indirect vdevs) is not drawn.
The repair write is drawn going down the tree once; in reality one repair child is created per bad side or column.

page.title: ZFS Scrub, Resilver and Rebuild
page.intro: This diagram answers the administrator's questions "what does a scrub or resilver actually do, why is it slow or fast, and how does a bad copy get repaired?". It follows a scan from `zpool scrub` through the ioctl into syncing context, where `dsl_scan_sync()` walks the pool's metadata once per txg, queues the data reads per top-level vdev, issues them in disk-offset order, and lets the mirror and raidz code repair any copy that fails its checksum. It shows how dirty time logs (DTLs) record what a device missed and limit a resilver to those txgs, how a second resilver is deferred, how a sequential rebuild differs, and what happens at completion.
